name: Grenada
snapshot: The "spice isle" of the Caribbean, governed since 2022 by Dickon Mitchell and still rebuilding Carriacou after Hurricane Beryl.
culture: Grenada produces much of the world's nutmeg, which appears on its flag. Spicemas, its carnival, features jab jab revellers covered in black oil and molasses, mocking colonial slaveholders. The country's history includes the 1979 revolution of Maurice Bishop and the US invasion of 1983 after his murder.
society: Tourism, nutmeg, cocoa and St George's University, a medical school for mainly American students, drive the economy. Hurricane Beryl in 2024 devastated Carriacou and Petite Martinique. Grenada's citizenship-by-investment programme brings in significant revenue.
situation: Dickon Mitchell, a lawyer, led the National Democratic Congress to victory in 2022, ending Keith Mitchell's long tenure. His government has focused on recovery and climate adaptation.
power: A parliamentary democracy and Commonwealth realm. The prime minister leads the majority in the 15-seat House of Representatives.

leaders.state: King Charles III, represented by a governor-general
